title: Chapel of St. Francis
subtitle: The Western Transept
description: A tranquil stone sanctuary bathed in azure light from high arched stained glass windows. Dedicated to the patron saint of creation.
clueHint: Look for where the golden sunlight casts cobalt blue rays onto the stone floor.

puzzle.question: Saint Francis of Assisi wrote a famous hymn praising creation. What is the celestial body he affectionately called 'Brother'?

options.feedback: Close! Wind is honored, but the primary celestial light is Brother Sun.
Spot on! In the Canticle of the Sun, he praises God for Sir Brother Sun.
Francis celebrated Sister Water, but the celestial brother was the Sun.
Nature is cherished, but the sun took top praise.

puzzle.funFact: St. Francis is known for staging the very first live Nativity scene in Greccio, Italy in 1223!

reward.itemDescription: A fragment of stained glass that glimmers with radiant cobalt energy.

title: The Ancient Cloister
subtitle: Courtyard Arcades
description: An open stone quadrangle surrounded by covered walkways where monks once walked in silent reflection.
clueHint: Find the quiet quadrangle surrounded by stone arches and a central olive tree.

puzzle.hintPhrase: A place of safety, holiness, and refuge from the world.
puzzle.funFact: In medieval times, anyone who reached a church sanctuary was granted legal protection from arrest!

reward.itemDescription: Hand-inked script inscribed with ancient monastic wisdom.

title: The Grand Bell Tower
subtitle: The Campanile
description: Towering 90 feet above the church roof, housing five bronze bells cast over a century ago.
clueHint: Look up to the tallest stone summit whose bells strike the hour.

puzzle.question: What is the specialized musical art of playing tuned church bells using a hand-lever keyboard called?

options.feedback: Correct! A carillon is an instrument of at least 23 cast bronze bells.
Clavier usually refers to a piano or harpsichord keyboard.
A cantata is a vocal composition with instrumental accompaniment.
Crescendo is a gradual increase in volume.

puzzle.funFact: The heaviest bell in this tower weighs over 3,200 pounds and is named 'Gabriel'!

reward.itemDescription: An ornate heavy key that unlocks the narrow staircase to the bell loft.

title: Garden of Gethsemane
subtitle: The Olive Grove Walk
description: A peaceful memorial garden planted with rosemary, lavender, and ancient olive shrubs.
clueHint: Follow the fragrance of sweet lavender toward the stone bench beneath the olive branches.

puzzle.hintPhrase: A period of keeping awake during the time usually spent sleeping, especially to pray.
puzzle.funFact: Some olive trees in the actual Garden of Gethsemane in Jerusalem have roots dated over 900 years old!

reward.itemDescription: A gleaming silver clasp symbolizing lasting peace and endurance.

title: The High Altar Mosaic
subtitle: Heart of the Nave
description: The sacred center of the cathedral featuring a breathtaking gold leaf Byzantine mosaic of Christ the Teacher.
clueHint: Walk down the main central nave aisle toward the grand gilded arch.

puzzle.hintPhrase: Aim your camera at the mosaic medallion above the altar, or scan the holy seal placed on the lectern.
puzzle.funFact: Over 45,000 tiny hand-cut Venetian glass tiles (tesserae) were laid to create this mosaic!

reward.itemDescription: A miniature ceremonial incense vessel that shines with pure gold luster.

title: The Crypt & Historical Archive
subtitle: Lower Vault Chambers
description: Subterranean vaulted chambers housing antique liturgical books, 19th-century records, and cornerstone memorabilia.
clueHint: Descend the curved stone stairs beneath the north choir loft.

puzzle.question: What sacred ancient language was used in the earliest hand-written copies of the New Testament Gospels?

options.feedback: Exact! Koine ('common') Greek was the universal lingua franca of the 1st century Mediterranean.
Latin became prominent later (e.g. the Vulgate), but the originals were in Greek.
Old English translations did not emerge until centuries later.
Akkadian was an ancient Mesopotamian cuneiform language.

puzzle.funFact: The oldest surviving fragment of the Gospel of John is preserved on papyrus no bigger than a business card!

reward.itemDescription: A heavy wax seal stamp bearing the cathedral crest and founding date 1888.
